question: If a sum on compound interest (compounded yearly) becomes three times in 4 years, then with the same interest rate, the sum will become 81 times in:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a sum becomes **x times** in **T years**, it becomes **xⁿ times** in **n × T years**.

Given: Sum becomes 3¹ times in **4 years** (x = 3, T = 4).

To find: Time to become **81 times**.

Since 81 = 3⁴, here n = 4.

Required time = n × T = 4 × 4 = 16 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 16 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Sum becomes 3 times in 4 years at **Compound Interest**.

**Formula Used:** A = P(1 + r/100)t

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eee5969bdb7634f857e3c6ef0e551a1d9cf0885f6909c4b1258cbc285128fd76.png] 

⇒ Case 1: 3P = P(1 + r/100)⁴

⇒ 3 = (1 + r/100)⁴ — (Equation 1)

⇒ Case 2: 81P = P(1 + r/100)t

⇒ 81 = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ (3)⁴ = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ [(1 + r/100)⁴]⁴ = (1 + r/100)t [From Eq. 1]

⇒ (1 + r/100)¹⁶ = (1 + r/100)t

⇒ t = 16 years

**∴ The correct answer is 16 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The amount A on a principal P for t years at rate r% compounded annually is A = P(1 + r/100)t.

Successive Growth in CI

In compound interest, the amount grows geometrically. If a sum doubles in T years, it becomes 2² times in 2T years, 2³ times in 3T years, and so on.

Rule of 72

A quick shortcut to estimate the time required to double an investment is T ≈ 72 ÷ r, where r is the annual interest rate.</p
